full_judgment: 24. The above decision was made in connection with the Inter-Provincial Trade Ordinance (IV of 1964). It was found that the legislature merely made a choice of the subject, that is, regulation of the movement of commodities between the provinces, but has not stated any policy or standard or any limitation on the exercise of the power. It did not indicate any principle for regulation of the movement of the goods. It simply gave unrestricted, undefined and unlimited power to regulate the movement of goods. But this is one of the relatively rare occasions when the Court made a real inquiry as to the presence of any legislative policy in the statute. Therefore, the cited case does not have any manner of application to the facts of the present case.
